description: Each such source's carried `schema` satisfies §3.2's schema-validity gate: every referenced type is defined, every field and argument has a type, no two types or directives share a name and no definition or extension repeats a field or argument name, input positions carry input types and output positions output types, at most one `schema` definition exists and any schema extension extends a defined schema, and the `query` root operation type is present and is an Object type.
notes: §3.2 gate 5. An absent mutation or subscription root is not gated (§3.3.1 makes them optional); it is a §5.2.1.1 validation failure handled by §5.

tests.description: valid type-system-language schema
valid introspection-result schema
schema without a query root operation type (§3.3.1)

content.schema: type User { id: ID! name: String }

tests.description: field of an undefined type
repeated field name in one definition

content.schema: type Query { status: String status: Int }

tests.description: input type in an output position

content.schema:
type Query { a: In }
input In { x: Int }

tests.description: output type in an input position

content.schema:
type Query { a(arg: User): String }
type User { id: ID! }

introspection result whose queryType names a scalar
